Heard Sri Ravi B. Patil, learned counsel for the petitioner, Smt. Arati Patil, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent Nos.1, 3 and 7 and Sri Krupa Sagar Patil, learned counsel for respondent Nos.2, 4, 5 and 6.
2.

Writ petition is filed with the following prayer:
"(a) issue a writ of mandamus directing the respondents Nos.1 to 7 to consider the grievance of the petitioner as per the representation dated 05.04.2019 as at Annexure-F.1, F.2, and F.3, thereby direct the respondents authorities to take appropriate steps for returning the land of the petitioner which is not been utilized for the purpose for which it was acquired in the interest of justice.

(b) Pass such other order/orders, directions as this Hon'ble Court deems fit in the circumstances of the case including an order as to the costs of the present writ petition, in the interest of justice and equity."
3. Grievance of the writ petitioner is that the entire land in Sy.No.22, measuring 22 acres, 27 guntas,
situated in NC: 2024:KHC-K:2287 Kembhavi village, Shorapur Taluk, Yadagir Distrit, owned by the petitioner, has been acquired by issuing notifications under Section 4 (1) and 6 (1) of the Land Acquisition Act, vide notification dated 24.08.1989.
4. Since the petitioner did not come forward to take the compensation, the compensation amount was kept in a RD account.

In the meantime, the petitioners have filed representations vide Annexures-F, F1 and F2 to the Deputy Commissioner, Managing Director KBJNL (Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigam Niyamith), Executive Engineer, IBC 1.
Said representations are not considered by the concerned.

5. Sri Krupa Sagar Patil, representing the KBJNL contends that under Rule 37 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Karnataka)
Rules, 2015, the petitioners have to file a necessary representation to the Secretary, Revenue Department of the Government of Karnataka.

sentences.text: The petitioners have also got the remedy of approaching the Revenue Secretary for redressal of their grievances.

Sri Ravi B Patil, learned counsel for the petitioner, in his reply contends that the representation already given vide Annexure-F, F1 and F2 may be forwarded to the Revenue Secretary instead of directing the writ petitioners.

7. Secretary, Revenue Department, Government of Karnataka, Shall consider F, F1 and F2 in accordance with Rule 37 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Karnataka) Rules, 2015.

"(a) issue a writ of mandamus directing the respondents Nos.1 to 7 to consider the grievance of the petitioner as per the representation dated 05.04.2019 as at Annexure-F.1, F.2, and F.3, thereby direct the respondents authorities to take appropriate steps for returning the land of the petitioner which is not been utilized for the purpose for which it was acquired in the interest of justice.
7. Secretary, Revenue Department, Government of Karnataka, Shall consider F, F1 and F2 in accordance with Rule 37 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Karnataka) Rules, 2015.
